name: Johann
title: Finding strength in a brother's bond
preview: After months of confusing symptoms, Johann leans on his older brother's steady support to navigate intense chemotherapy cycles.
body_text:
Johann’s health concerns began in November of last year with dizziness and severe headaches. Initial ER visits and blood tests showed no major issues, and in December, he was treated for the flu. But his symptoms kept returning: fevers, hot flashes, and persistent fatigue. Another ER visit led to scans that revealed a spot on his chest. He was quickly transferred to the Children’s Hospital for further testing. It was there that Johann was diagnosed with Leukemia.

Johann undergoes chemotherapy in four-day cycles, followed by two weeks of rest, repeating this process until the round is complete. Once this phase ends, his care team will determine the next best course of treatment. He also receives steroids to help manage his emotions during therapy. Throughout it all, Johann is supported by his older brother, who looks out for him with care and compassion, something Johann deeply appreciates.

Like many families facing a serious diagnosis, Johann’s family was unprepared for the sudden changes that followed. Mom had to leave her job to become his full-time caregiver, leaving his father as the sole provider. This shift has brought significant financial challenges. Your generosity and support are greatly appreciated this holiday season!

name: Darla
title: Darla's brave journey through leukemia
preview: Enduring intense leukemia treatments, Darla relies on the love of her family to stay strong as they navigate overwhelming hardships together.
body_text:
It began on vacation when Darla felt pain in her elbow. After returning home, the pain worsened, and her elbow swelled, prompting a visit to the ER. Tests showed an infection, and she was sent home. But when inflammation spread to her wrist and ankle, they returned to the ER for more tests. Referred to hematology, the family received the devastating diagnosis: Darla had Leukemia.

Darla now undergoes chemotherapy through a chest port four days a week, along with weekly lumbar punctures. She hasn’t been able to attend school during treatment, which has been especially hard for her as she often feels sad about missing out. Thankfully, she’s surrounded by love and support, which gives her the strength to keep pushing through this difficult journey.

At the time of her diagnosis, Darla’s dad was injured and unable to work, and the family was struggling on limited income from her mom. When her mom had to stop working to care for her full-time. a significant financial hardship fell upon the family, adding to the emotional weight of Darla’s journey. Thank you for your heartfelt generosity during this special time of year!

name: Alice
title: Alice's brave fight against leukemia
preview: Facing a difficult leukemia diagnosis, Alice works hard in therapy to regain her strength as her family navigates this challenging chapter.
body_text:
When Alice’s mom first noticed a lump on her neck, they visited Children’s Hospital Los Angeles, where doctors initially believed it was just an enlarged lymph node and prescribed medication. After a month without improvement and the development of a persistent fever two months later, Alice was brought back for further testing. Bloodwork and additional evaluations confirmed the difficult news that Alice had leukemia.

Alice currently undergoes weekly chemotherapy treatments administered through a chest port and attends weekly physical therapy sessions to rebuild her strength and mobility. Once she regains enough strength, she will begin homeschooling to continue her education at her own pace.

Alice’s diagnosis has placed a significant financial strain on the family. With her stepfather as the only source of income, balancing household expenses while managing her care has been incredibly challenging. The family deeply appreciates your generosity and support this holiday season.

name: Marie
title: Marie's bright future after beating leukemia
preview: After defeating leukemia, Marie is pursuing medicine in college as her family builds a stable, hopeful future in a new home.
body_text:
One day Marie ’s father grew concerned after she began experiencing sudden eyesight problems . Marie's condition progressed and her family sought medical attention. Doctors were unable to diagnose her, and she was promptly sent home. A few weeks later she attended a follow-up appointment , and her family was informed that she was diagnosed with Leukemia.

Marie began treatment immediately. Thankfully today, after a long treatment journey, she is Cancer free! However, the family experienced financial hardships throughout Marie’s treatment. Father was unable to maintain his job due to being a single parent and having to attend all of Marie’s appointments. The family also lost their home prompting them to move into Miracle Manor.

Fortunately, the family has had positive moments in their lives since then! Marie is now a college student, pursuing a career in the medical field while Patricio, her Dad, landed a position as Lead Technician at Regency Plumbing through our partnership with Merge. The family has now moved into an apartment of their own, and enjoying every moment of their new chapter.

name: Greyson
title: Greyson's ongoing battle for every breath
preview: After surviving 210 days in the NICU and a sudden cardiac arrest, baby Greyson and his parents continue their brave fight for his future.
body_text:
Greyson was born a micro-premature baby with underdeveloped lungs, which required him to spend 210 days in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). After being discharged, he contracted two viral infections that brought him back to the hospital. In March 2024, Greyson was admitted to CHOC and diagnosed with a serious condition following a cardiac arrest.

Since then, Greyson has undergone invasive, high-risk surgeries and has struggled to breathe on his own. His parents often feel emotionally drained and fearful of what lies ahead.

Dad is self-employed but has had to cancel several jobs to care for Greyson and attend his medical appointments, while family and friends have helped support the family financially. Mom and Dad strive to stay strong for their children and each other. The Remus family is deeply grateful for the support from Miracles for Kids and would greatly appreciate your generosity this holiday season.

name: Benbarry
title: Benbarry's triumph over sickle cell
preview: After battling sickle cell and a tough transplant recovery, Benbarry is now thriving as his family embraces a stable, hopeful future.
body_text:
Benbarry was born in Kenya and was a healthy baby until concerns arose at eight months old. After his parents sought a second opinion, he was diagnosed with sickle cell anemia at just 18 months old. Now living in California and while awaiting an asylum interview, he underwent a stem cell transplant with his sister as a perfect donor match and received close medical care during recovery. Recovery was physically and emotionally challenging for Benbarry. Because he was severely immunocompromised, he was isolated at home, attended school online, and was unable to participate in many activities with his peers. He often felt discouraged about being smaller, but his inner strength and positive attitude continued to inspire his family.

Fortunately, Benbarry is now doing well. He can do physical activities and is attending the gym. Mom says he is doing things he has never done before and is happy!

During his treatment journey, the family faced many financial challenges. Mom was the full-time caregiver while Dad was the sole income earner. Through Miracles for Kids’ partnership with Merge, Mom secured a position as an Executive Assistant/Board Liaison at the Community Foundation in Sonoma County, bringing renewed hope for their future. They are deeply grateful for every act of kindness.

name: Leonel
title: Leonel's journey to save his vision
preview: Now free from chemotherapy, Leonel faces a crucial surgery to save his sight as the Casillas family begins a hopeful new chapter.
body_text:
In taking the next steps forward to bettering Leonel’s health, the doctors recommend eye surgery. There is a possibility of him losing his vision completely. Mom and Dad want to prevent Leonel’s vison loss and plan on going forward with the eye surgery. Leonel has become more active, and the family feels much better knowing he is stable and free from having to do chemotherapy treatment.

Dad is working full-time and is the only source of income. With the transition of treatment, Mom is staying home to care for Leonel and her other children so that they can adjust to their new lifestyle. With the new chapter, the Casillas family is excited to start their life back up again and regain financial stability. The Casillas family appreciates your generosity and support during this holiday season!

name: Jeremiah
title: Jeremiah's family kept their home through crisis
preview: Jeremiah has Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis. Facing eviction, his mother Maria received emergency rental assistance and kept their home.
body_text:
(March 2026) – At just four months old, Jeremiah began showing signs that something wasn’t right — frequent ear infections, unusual rashes, and a relentless cycle of illness that left his mother, Maria, searching desperately for answers. For nearly a year, appointment after appointment brought more questions than clarity. Then one day, Jeremiah’s stomach suddenly swelled. Terrified, Maria rushed him to the hospital, where extensive testing finally revealed the cause: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis, a rare disorder that can damage tissue and organs throughout the body. Treatment began immediately.

For Maria, a single mother of six and a caregiver for the elderly, life did not pause for a diagnosis. She balanced hospital visits, long work shifts, and the daily needs of her other children — holding everything together through sheer love and determination. Then another crisis struck. An eviction notice arrived. She had less than 30 days to pay her rent or lose the only home her family had.

It was during a routine monthly check-in that Maria’s caseworker learned just how urgent things had become. That conversation set everything in motion. Working alongside one of our trusted community partners, The Change Reaction , emergency rental assistance was secured — just in time. That support didn’t just keep a roof over her family’s heads. It gave Maria permission to breathe, to be present at Jeremiah’s bedside, and to focus on healing instead of survival.

What happened next speaks to the kind of family Maria is raising. Even amid their own hardship, she and Jeremiah chose to give back — quietly purchasing groceries for their elderly neighbor. No fanfare. No recognition sought. Just grace, offered freely by a family that knows what it means to need help and chooses, despite everything, to extend it to others.

Today, because of the generosity of supporters like you, Maria can focus on what matters most: Jeremiah’s healing and her children’s stability. A caseworker who listened. A partner organization that moved quickly. A donor community that made it all possible. Each involvement mattered. Yours does too.

Jeremiah’s story is not the only one.

Right now, there are families in our community struggling with a critically-ill child facing a devastating diagnosis, an eviction notice, or a moment of crisis — just one compassionate act away from finding their footing again. Your gift to Miracles for Kids ensures that when those moments come, no family faces them alone. Every dollar you give is a lifeline.

name: Abraham
title: Abraham is growing stronger toward a transplant
preview: Born with renal failure and Potter sequence, 3-year-old Abraham is working toward a kidney transplant as his single mom raises three kids.
body_text:
(June 2026) – Meet 3-Year-Old Abraham, diagnosed with Renal Failure and Potter sequence before birth. Despite significant medical challenges from the very beginning, Abraham continues to defy the odds and grow stronger each day as he works toward becoming eligible for a life-changing kidney transplant.

In the meantime, Abraham requires ongoing medical care and frequent hospital visits. As a single mother, his mom works tirelessly to balance his complex medical needs while caring for his two siblings at home.

Despite the challenges he faces, Abraham is full of joy and loves being around people. His bright smile and resilient spirit bring light to everyone around him, especially during difficult days. While Abraham has made tremendous progress, his journey is far from over. Before he can receive a kidney transplant, doctors want to see him continue to grow and gain strength. Every milestone is hard-earned, and every step forward represents months of dedication, appointments, treatments, and unwavering love from his family.

The demands of caring for a medically fragile child have also created significant financial strain. As a single mother, balancing hospital stays, medical appointments, and the needs of three children can be overwhelming. Like many Miracles for Kids families, Abraham’s family faces challenges that extend far beyond his diagnosis.

Thanks to supporters like you, Miracles for Kids helps provide stability during these difficult times, allowing families to focus on what matters most—the treatment of their child.

Abraham’s family is deeply grateful for the support they have received and for the community that continues to walk alongside them on this journey. Your generosity helps make stories like Abraham’s possible, providing stability, relief, and the reminder that no family has to face a critical illness alone.

Meet Jaxxon’s Family – One of Our 2026 Angel Flight Families!

Jaxxon was born with biliary atresia, a fatal liver disease, and received a life-saving liver transplant at just 2 years old. The years of intensive care that followed required his mom to step away from work, leaving his dad as the sole provider for the family of six. Jaxxon, now 5 years olld, was able to go to school last year for the very first time, a miracle for him and his family!

title: Julio is building his future after aplastic anemia
preview: Diagnosed with Aplastic Anemia at 9, Julio is now 20 and back with Miracles for Kids, building a career through an apprenticeship.

Meet Julio- One of Our 2026 Angel Flights!

When he was 9, Julio was diagnosed with Aplastic Anemia. His little sister was his bone marrow donor at just 2 years old. name: Alexander
title: Alexander finished treatment for a rare cancer
preview: At 15, Alexander completed chemo and radiation for Rhabdomyosarcoma. With his stepfather out of work, Miracles helps cover the bills.
body_text:
(July 2026) – What started as a day of playing with his cousins quickly turned into a life-changing moment for 15-year-old Alexander. After complaining of severe tooth pain and not feeling well, his mother took him to the emergency room. There, doctors discovered a mass in his head. Soon after, Alexander was diagnosed with Rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare but aggressive form of cancer.

Alexander faced months of intensive treatment with remarkable courage. He completed both chemotherapy and radiation, but while treatment has ended, his journey is far from over. He continues to attend monthly follow-up appointments, with regular scans, biopsies, and MRIs every three months to closely monitor his recovery. Thankfully, his doctors feel encouraged by his progress and have even begun discussing the possibility of removing his port, a milestone his family has been hoping for.

As Alexander continues to heal, his family is also navigating the lasting financial challenges that often accompany a childhood cancer diagnosis. His mother remains by his side throughout his recovery while caring for her other children at home. At the same time his stepfather, the family’s sole provider, recently missed two months of work while recovering from a serious leg injury. As a day laborer with inconsistent income, every missed paycheck places additional strain on the family’s ability to cover basic household expenses.

During this difficult time, Miracles for Kids has helped ease their burden by providing financial assistance through the Lifeline Program and essential support through the Boost Program , allowing Alexander’s family to focus on what matters most — his continued recovery and well-being.

Today, Alexander’s family remains hopeful for the future and deeply grateful for the community standing beside them. Thanks to compassionate supporters like you, families facing the unimaginable don’t have to face it alone. Your generosity provides stability, hope, and the reassurance that, even in life’s most difficult moments, someone is there to help carry the load.

name: Mariah
title: Mariah is fighting a tumor in her jaw
preview: For two years Mariah’s mouth pain went unexplained, until a cancerous jaw tumor was found. Her single mom cut back work to care for her.
body_text:
(August 2026) – For two years, Mariah endured constant mouth pain and swelling while her family searched for answers. After numerous dental visits, a referral to a specialist finally led to the heartbreaking discovery of a cancerous tumor in her jaw.

Mariah’s treatment includes chemotherapy both at home and in the hospital, with daily oral medication and regular biopsies to monitor her progress. She has also been diagnosed with TMJ, limiting her ability to open her mouth, and surgery may be needed to remove the tumor and improve her jaw function. Through the pain, treatments, and uncertainty, Mariah continues to find reasons to smile with the support of her loving family.

For Mariah’s mother, a single parent, caring for her daughter also brings significant financial challenges. Reducing her work schedule from full-time to part-time allows her to be there for Mariah’s care, but makes it increasingly difficult to keep up with the family’s everyday expenses.

Miracles for Kids helps families like Mariah’s navigate the financial and emotional challenges that accompany a child’s serious illness. Through the generosity of donors and supporters like you, families receive critical assistance that helps ease the burden and allows them to focus on what matters most—their child.

Every gift helps Miracles for Kids provide hope, stability, and critical support to more families facing childhood illness.

name: Alexia
title: Alexia lives with severe epilepsy at ten
preview: At 10, Alexia lives with a rare, severe epilepsy and receives palliative care. Her brother Javier has the same condition.
body_text:
(August 2026) – Meet 10-year-old Alexia, who was diagnosed with Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome, a rare and severe form of epilepsy, at just three years old. The condition causes frequent and intense seizures and has significantly affected her development. One particularly severe episode required hospitalization and intubation, after which Alexia was placed in palliative care.

Alexia is nonverbal and depends on a feeding pump, G-tube, supplemental oxygen, and ongoing care from multiple medical specialists. Because she cannot communicate verbally, her mother has learned to recognize subtle expressions and sounds that indicate when Alexia is uncomfortable or in pain.

Alexia’s diagnosis is only part of this family’s story. Her older brother, Javier, has the same rare condition and also receives palliative care. Caring for two medically fragile children around the clock has made it impossible for their parents to maintain employment, creating tremendous emotional, physical, and financial strain.

Amid that uncertainty, Miracles for Kids helps provide support that eases some of the family’s financial burden, allowing Alexia’s parents to remain focused on the complex needs of their children.

For families like Alexia’s, support extends far beyond financial assistance. It provides stability during circumstances few families could ever anticipate and reminds them that they do not have to navigate the challenges of childhood illness alone.

name: Isaias
title: Isaias faces leukemia after losing his home
preview: Days after the LA fires took their home, 7-year-old Isaias was diagnosed with leukemia. His single mom is fighting to keep going.
body_text:
(March 2025) – Before learning of his diagnosis, Isaias’ family had been dealing with the loss of their home due to the recent Los Angeles fires . The following morning after the family was ordered to evacuate, Isaias, age 7, woke up with inflamed gums and cheeks. He first went to a dentist and received antibiotics. However, as the infection grew worse, two specialists referred them to CHLA, which is where bloodwork and additional tests discovered Isaias had Leukemia.

As a single parent to two children, it has been increasingly difficult for Isaia’s mom to balance the responsibilities of losing her home while learning about Isaias’ treatment. Thankfully a close relative has allowed them to reside in their home for the time being until suitable housing is found. Since his diagnosis, Isaias has undergone multiple rounds of chemo, lumbar punctures, and blood transfusions to lessen his painful symptoms.

As a housekeeper, Isaia’s mom has not been able to return to work since the fires and his diagnosis. The family has managed to get by with the help of other family members. Isaias’ mother is extremely grateful for all the support Miracles for Kids has provided to her and her children.

name: Emerson
title: Emerson has been in the hospital since birth
preview: Born with a heart valve that would not shut, baby Emerson has been hospitalized since birth as his family holds on to hope.
body_text:
(April 2025) – Emerson was born at Holy Cross Hospital but was transferred to Children’s Hospital Los Angeles because he had a whistling sound in his heart. Immediately after being transferred, the medical team planned to operate on his heart since one of his valves would not shut. However, the doctors decided to wait and to prescribe medication instead.

After some time, the valve closed by itself. Unfortunately, the doctors found problems in his respiratory system and diagnosed him with respiratory failure called Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia Organ Acute Disease . Due to this complication, Emerson has been hospitalized since birth.

Emerson and his family were recently approved to receive a grant from Miracles for Kids towards their monthly car payment. This has helped them secure transportation to critically-needed doctor appointments and treatments.

Emerson’s family is extremely grateful for the help they are receiving from Miracles for Kids and especially wishes to thank those who donate to help families like theirs.

name: Emiliano
title: Emiliano was born with a fragile heart
preview: Born with four holes in his heart, baby Emiliano faces surgery, fighting with strength as his family stays close.
body_text:
(May 2025) – Emiliano was born at 43 weeks and was immediately taken to the NICU. After birth, his mother learned that he had multiple heart defects—four holes in his heart, one of them significantly large, along with a narrow valve that also required surgery.

These issues, though large enough to be detected during pregnancy, had gone unnoticed. At just eight days old, doctors detected a heart murmur. On February 11th, a pulmonary band was placed in his heart to limit blood flow.

Though Emiliano was briefly discharged in December, he was soon readmitted due to high potassium levels. Since then, he’s faced multiple hospital stays, including a battle with RSV. Now, Emiliano remains in the hospital under close observation. His condition is critical, and he is considered high-risk. His medical team is still deciding whether to repair the valve or the heart defect first.

Through it all, Emiliano continues to fight with incredible strength, surrounded by the love and hope of his family. Emiliano and his family have been approved to receive a grant from Miracles for Kids for rent and they are extremely grateful to all the supporters who help make this possible. The assistance has truly been a miracle for Emiliano and his family.

name: Willow
title: Willow faces a rare disorder with a big smile
preview: Diagnosed with a rare genetic disorder as a baby, Willow faces daily therapies, her bright smile keeping her family strong.
body_text:
(June 2025) – Willow was born just three weeks into the national COVID shutdown. Initially, her birth did not raise any significant concerns. However, by the time she was four weeks old, her parents observed unusual movements.

Due to strict COVID restrictions, they first shared a video of these irregularities with their doctor, which led to an immediate in-person consultation. After a series of examinations, baby Willow was diagnosed with a rare genetic disorder.

Currently, she undergoes various therapies and takes medication to manage her condition, as no definitive treatment has been found. Despite the challenges, her family remains hopeful for a breakthrough in treatment.

Surrounded by the love of her parents and sisters, Willow’s smile serves as a source of strength for her family. Additionally, Miracles for Kids provides support by assisting with a portion of their car payment, which provides transportation stability in moments of unexpected urgent hospital and clinic visits. The family is extremely grateful for the help they receive.

name: John B
title: John has fought for his heart for nine years
preview: Born with half a working heart, 9-year-old John has spent 16 months in the hospital. Now in hospice, he's surrounded by love.
body_text:
(July 2025) – John, now 9 years old, was diagnosed with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome while his mother was seven months pregnant. At just two days old, he endured his first open-heart surgery, followed by a second at nine months.

As he grew, doctors discovered his left lung wasn’t developing properly, making him ineligible for the third surgery in his planned series. In 2019, after years of uncertainty, John was placed on the heart transplant list. Not long after, he began coughing up blood. A pulmonary tear was discovered, and the complication led to the heartbreaking removal of John from the transplant list.

John has now spent over 16 months in the hospital. When doctors at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles could do no more, his mother reached out to six other hospitals, holding onto hope. Sadly, each gave the same difficult answer. Today, John is in hospice care, surrounded by love and his family’s unbreakable strength.

To help ease the financial burden during this extremely difficult time, Miracles for Kids is covering the family’s rent through the Lifeline Program – so they can focus on John.

name: Vincent Jr
title: Vincent is battling rare Hunter syndrome
preview: At six months old, Vincent was diagnosed with rare Hunter Syndrome. His first-time parents are fighting for his future.
body_text:
(August 2025) – Vincent Jr. was born without any signs of medical concern, until his parents received an unexpected call just days after bringing him home. The hospital asked them to return immediately for further testing. After a series of evaluations, doctors confirmed a rare diagnosis – Hunter Syndrome.

Now just six months old, Vincent is considered high-risk and requires weekly enzyme replacement therapy. His care team is hopeful that he may qualify for a stem cell transplant, but his strength and stability must improve before moving forward.

As first-time parents, the diagnosis has been overwhelming. Dad has taken a leave of absence to support Mom and care for Vincent full time. To help ease the financial strain, Miracles for Kids Lifeline Program is covering the family’s car payment — ensuring they have safe, reliable transportation for Vincent’s frequent and urgent medical appointments.

name: Amethyst
title: Amethyst's family was reunited by hope
preview: Diagnosed with leukemia at age three, Amethyst and her family were split apart, then reunited near her hospital through Miracles.
body_text:
(September 2025) – At only three years old, Amethyst has faced more medical challenges than most will in a lifetime. After being diagnosed with leukemia, she began an intense treatment journey expected to last two to three years. To ensure she could receive the specialized care she needed, her family made a life-changing decision—Amethyst and her mother relocated from their military base to her grandparents’ home, leaving behind her father and older brother. With the family split across state lines, Amethyst’s care became her mother’s full-time responsibility.

The emotional and financial strain of her diagnosis quickly became overwhelming. That’s when Miracles for Kids stepped in. Through the Lifeline Program , the family received critical support to help cover essential bills. Most recently, they joined the Safe Haven Program , which provides subsidized housing for families facing severe financial hardship due to a child’s illness. Today, the family lives together, reunited at Miracle Manor, just minutes from the hospital—no longer separated by circumstance.

Ongoing assistance from Miracles for Kids helps cover housing and car payments, easing the financial burden so Amethyst’s family can focus on what matters most: her healing. Their story is a powerful reminder of how vital stability, proximity, and support are during times of medical crisis.

name: Christian
title: Christian lives with a rare genetic disorder
preview: Six-year-old Christian lives with a rare genetic disorder and daily chemo. His dad leans on Miracles to keep the family afloat.
body_text:
(October 2025) – Christian was diagnosed with a rare genetic disorder before his birth, a condition that has a history in his mother’s family. His parents collaborated closely with their doctor and underwent various tests during the pregnancy to prepare for potential outcomes. Their worst fears were confirmed when doctors diagnosed Christian with Neurofibromatosis Type 1. ‍

Now six years old, he faces numerous daily challenges, including an inability to digest liquids or solid foods independently, relying entirely on medical assistance. A mutation on chromosome 17 causes his body to produce abnormal proteins, and he is currently undergoing chemotherapy in an effort to slow the disorder’s progression.

Having spent much of his young life in hospitals, Christian experiences significant anxiety at the prospect of additional hospital stays. To alleviate some of the family’s financial burden, Miracles for Kids is assisting by covering part of their rent through Bill Pay in our Lifeline Program , providing Christian’s father with essential support as he strives to care for his family during this challenging time.

name: Sebastian
title: Sebastian is fighting a brain tumor at 18
preview: At 18, Sebastian lost his sight, hearing, and ability to walk to a brain tumor. His single mom now cares for him full-time.
body_text:
(November 2025) – For months, 18-year-old Sebastian experienced alarming symptoms—hearing strange noises, losing his vision, and struggling to walk—while doctors searched for answers. After numerous appointments and growing concern, an MRI finally revealed the cause: a brain tumor. He was rushed to the hospital for emergency surgery.

Around the same time, Sebastian lost his ability to see, hear, and walk. Since then, his mother and younger siblings have devoted themselves to his care. His recovery from brain surgery has been long and difficult, and he is now undergoing chemotherapy. He also takes medication to relieve pressure caused by the tumor, with the hope that treatment will shrink the mass and ease his symptoms.

Sebastian’s diagnosis has reshaped life for the entire family. A dependable helper at home, he often stepped in like a second parent, supporting his mom while she worked. Now, those roles have reversed as the family navigates a new reality—leaning on one another and facing each day together.

Sebastian’s mother, a single parent, has had to step away from work to provide full-time care. While her eldest child helps when possible, the family is under significant financial strain.

Miracles for Kids is proud to support them by helping alleviate their housing expenses through the Lifeline Program , allowing the family to focus on what matters most: Sebastian’s healing and recovery.

name: Dailani
title: Dailani is fighting cancer at just two
preview: At just two, Dailani is battling a rare cancer. After losing their home, her family is living in a shelter as she fights to heal.
body_text:
(December 2025) – At just two years old, little Dailani has already faced more than most children her age. Her journey began with repeated emergency room visits after her mother noticed concerning changes in her health and alarming digestive symptoms. When answers remained unclear, her mom advocated for further testing. That persistence led to the life-changing diagnosis of rhabdomyosarcoma, a rare cancer that affects soft tissue and skeletal muscles.

Soon after diagnosis, Dailani underwent surgery that required the removal of her bladder and began weekly chemotherapy treatments. Despite side effects such as nausea, digestive complications, and limited mobility, she continues treatment with remarkable strength, supported by a family hopeful for healing and remission.

As Dailani fights for her health, her family faces overwhelming challenges. In addition to extended hospital stays, the family endured frequent travel from Las Vegas, where her dad worked, to Children’s Hospital Los Angeles to ensure Dailani received the specialized care she needed. The demands of constant appointments ultimately led to her father losing his job, followed by the heartbreaking loss of their home. Today, the family is living in a shelter as they work toward stability.

Dailani’s family connected with Miracles for Kids in November and is now working with case managers to access additional services. In the meantime, immediate support is being provided through critically-needed grocery gift cards – helping ensure the family can afford nourishing meals during this difficult time. This early assistance offers immediate relief when it is needed most.

name: Remington
title: Remington is fighting cancer as a baby
preview: At one year old, Remington was diagnosed with aggressive cancer. His parents are stretched thin as Miracles helps cover the bills.
body_text:
(January 2026) – One morning, Remington woke up with watery eyes that worsened throughout the day. Initial hospital evaluations showed nothing alarming, but just days later, one of his eyes began to bulge noticeably. His family rushed him back to the hospital, where a CT scan revealed devastating news — two tumors.

At only 1 year old, Remington was diagnosed with Acute Neuroblastoma, a rare and aggressive cancer. His young life is now filled with chemotherapy, radiation, and seven daily medications. At his age, he cannot understand the diagnosis — only that his days now include frequent hospital visits, procedures, and unfamiliar routines.

The diagnosis has placed significant financial strain on the family. Remington’s father left his job to become his full-time caregiver, while his mother continues working to support the household. With only one income, meeting basic needs has become increasingly difficult. Miracles for Kids is helping the family with a grant to cover essential expenses such as water, power, and gas, providing stability during an incredibly challenging time.

Miracles for Kids has also brought moments of comfort and connection. Recently, Remington and his family attended a wellness event hosted by the Miracles for Kids Balance Program in partnership with Lemons to Lemonade, a nonprofit focused on grief support. The event included lunch, games, raffles, face painting, and thoughtful gifts, along with essential items and gift cards.

As the day came to a close, the family’s gratitude was unmistakable — a reminder that compassion, community, and support can make a meaningful difference, even in the hardest moments. Through programs like these, Miracles for Kids continues to stand beside families like Remington’s, offering care, stability, and hope when it’s needed most.

name: Efren
title: Efren had a brain tumor removed at age three
preview: At three, Eren had a 5cm brain tumor removed and now faces chemo. Both parents paused work to stay by his hospital bed.
body_text:
(February 2026) – At the age of three, Efren was rushed to the emergency room following a head injury. Imaging and tests uncovered a brain mass, resulting in immediate hospitalization. Within 72 hours, he underwent surgery to remove a 5cm tumor, with 98% of it successfully excised. His recovery proved to be arduous. He spent several weeks intubated due to respiratory complications and was unable to eat or move for nearly three months.

Once stabilized, Efren was moved to the oncology unit, where he was diagnosed with Medulloblastoma, a fast-growing, cancerous brain tumor. He is currently receiving chemotherapy through a port and a Broviac line, along with various medications to manage side effects, protect his liver, alleviate pain, and maintain his blood counts.

Efren will remain hospitalized through the completion of this treatment cycle. During this difficult time, both parents have taken leave from work to stay by his side, relying on savings while facing growing financial strain. Through Miracles for Kids, the family has found meaningful relief and stability as they navigate this challenging chapter. Assistance through the Lifeline Program is helping cover the family’s car payments, easing one burden so they can focus fully on Efren’s care and recovery.

name: Postino
title: Postino is waiting for a new heart
preview: Seven-year-old Postino has lived in a hospital for five months, a machine keeping his heart beating as he awaits a transplant.
body_text:
(March 2026) – It began with something small, an unusual tiredness, a quiet complaint of weakness. Then one day, five-year-old Postino Jr. mentioned that he couldn’t feel his feet. In that single moment, his mother knew, with the certainty only a parent could feel, that something was terribly wrong.

She didn’t wait. She trusted her instincts, gathered her son, and rushed him to the hospital. After hours of tests, uncertainty, and the kind of waiting that stretches every minute into an eternity, she received the news no parent is ever prepared to hear: Postino’s heart was failing.

Before his sixth birthday, Postino had already endured two open-heart surgeries. Each procedure carried hope. Each time, his family held their breath and prayed. But his small body rejected both, and now Postino finds himself in the most critical chapter of his young life, fighting with a courage and resilience that humbles everyone around him.

Postino is seven now, and for the past five months, he has lived inside a hospital room, tethered to a Left Ventricular Assist Device – a machine that keeps his fragile heart beating while he waits. He is currently listed as 1A status for a heart transplant, the highest priority level on the national waitlist. Every day is a gift. Every day is also a vigil.

And yet, behind that hospital room door, there is more than fear. There is a mother – fierce, devoted, and unbreakable – who refuses to leave her son’s side. As a single parent to four children, she divides herself daily between Postino’s bedside and her children at home, doing everything within her power to hold her family together. Since Postino’s hospitalization, she has had to stop working entirely, surviving now on government assistance alone. The bills don’t pause for a mother’s grief. The electricity doesn’t stay on out of sympathy.

That is where Miracles for Kids stepped in.

By covering this family’s electricity bill, Miracles for Kids did something that goes far beyond a financial transaction. It sent a message to a mother in the depths of her darkest season: You are not invisible. You are not alone. We see you, and we are with you.

That is what your support makes possible. Not just paid bills but the profound reassurance that someone cares, that this family matters, that Postino’s fight matters.

Postino is still waiting for his miracle. His family is still holding on.

You have the power to be part of their story. A donation to Miracles for Kids today helps ensure that families do not have to face impossible choices alone and that while they fight for their child’s life, we are fighting with them.

name: Leonardo
title: Leonardo was born with half a heart
preview: Baby Leonardo was born with only half a working heart. After two surgeries, his single mom cares for him around the clock.
body_text:
(May 2026) – Leonardo is just 6 months old, but he has already survived more than most will face in a lifetime. At 18 weeks pregnant, Leonardo’s mom learned that her baby had a severe congenital heart defect. From that day forward, she met with specialists, attended countless appointments, and prepared herself for the complex medical journey ahead. Every step was heavy, but she carried it with unwavering love.

When Leonardo was born, he was rushed straight to the NICU at CHOC Hospital. Doctors confirmed that only half of his heart was functioning — a condition requiring multiple surgeries and lifelong care. Before she could bring him home, his mom completed extensive medical training so she could safely care for him on her own.

Leonardo had his first surgery shortly after birth. In January, he endured a second open heart surgery to repair additional complications, including a leaking valve. The procedure was successful, and today he continues to recover under close medical supervision.

Leonardo’s daily care is intense. He takes multiple medications, receives injections, and participates in at-home physical therapy. Every week, Leonardo and his mom travel long distances for follow up appointments to monitor his heart.

As a single mother, Leonardo’s mom had to stop working to care for him full time. With limited savings and ongoing medical demands, the financial strain has been overwhelming.

This is where Miracles for Kids — and donors like you — make all the difference.

Thanks to your generosity, Miracles for Kids is able to help support Leonardo and his family by paying their car insurance through the Life Line Program Bill Pay Assistance. This aid ensures she can get Leonardo to his appointments safely and consistently. It may seem like a small thing, but for this family, it is life sustaining.

name: Alexa
title: Alexa is on a leukemia journey at 14
preview: At 14, Alexa was diagnosed with leukemia. As her single mom of five focused on her care, Miracles helped ease the strain.
body_text:
(June 2026) – What started as back pain and persistent headaches quickly turned into every parent’s nightmare. After a series of tests revealed severe anemia, 14-year-old Alexa was diagnosed with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), beginning a treatment journey that would change life for her entire family.

Following her diagnosis, Alexa underwent chemotherapy and faced the challenges that come with intensive treatment, including taking multiple medications each day. The physical and emotional toll of her illness disrupted many aspects of daily life, including her education, which led her to transition to homeschooling.

For Alexa’s mother, a single parent raising five children, the diagnosis brought challenges that extended far beyond the hospital. As she focused her time and energy on supporting Alexa’s health and well-being, the family faced mounting financial pressures and uncertainty that so often accompanies a serious childhood illness.

During one of the most difficult chapters of their lives, Miracles for Kids was able to provide critical support, helping ease their financial burden and allowing the family to focus on what mattered most. Today, Alexa and her family remain deeply grateful for the stability, generosity, and hope they found through the support of donors like you.

title: Kimberly faced illness and homelessness
preview: Born with Down syndrome and a fragile heart, 3-year-old Kimberly faced homelessness with her mom, until Miracles stepped in.
body_text: Kimberly was born with Trisomy 21 and has fought through severe heart complications. At just three years old, she has undergone two surgeries, and will require many more.
